answer: Jade cannot be minted, only earned, so standing must be ground out. Each identity needs two holders outside its own inlet to countersign its bead, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct witnesses rather than one friendly crew. Each bead is priced by rank: the k-th bead an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A glacier audit replays a random bead each epoch, and an unconfirmed bead melts the whole inlet and forfeits its bonds, which cannot be pooled, lent or resold.
